name: Egg Foo Young
assumptions: Recipe makes 4 omelets explicitly stated in instructions, each served over rice as a complete dish; yield therefore 4 servings.
Total active + passive time (gravy ~5 min, batter ~5 min, frying 4 omelets ~20 min including cooling, plus rice cooking) conservatively estimated at 45 minutes.
Oyster sauce classified as containing shellfish (true) and ambiguous for fish (null).
Soy sauce classified as containing wheat (true) and soy (true); oyster sauce also contains soy (true).
Shaoxing wine, pepper, salt, sugar, oil, rice, and cornstarch introduce no listed allergens.
Spring onions and bean sprouts introduce no listed allergens.
No dairy, tree nuts, peanuts, or sesame in listed ingredients (confidently absent).
Gluten-free is null because soy sauce and oyster sauce are typically not certified gluten-free and often contain wheat; no explicit gluten-free ingredients or certification mentioned.
Pescatarian true because all ingredients are compatible with pescatarian diet (includes seafood, eggs, no meat).
Vegetarian and vegan false due to shrimp, beef stock, oyster sauce, and eggs.
instructions:
Make the gravy:
In a small saucepan, add the beef stock, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, oyster sauce, and white pepper powder over medium heat. Whisk together and bring to a simmer. 

Combine the cornstarch and water in a small bowl and whisk to dissolve. Add to the saucepan and whisk until the gravy thickens and coats the back of the spoon, 2 to 3 minutes. Cover the saucepan with a lid and keep it warm on the lowest possible heat.

Make the egg foo young batter:
In a medium bowl, whisk together the cornstarch and water until dissolved. Add the eggs, salt, and sugar. Whisk until well combined and there are no more egg white clumps. 

Add the green onion, bean sprouts, and shrimp. Stir until everything is evenly coated.

Fry the egg foo young:
Add the vegetable oil to a large wok; it should reach about 2 inches up the sides. Heat the oil over medium-high heat to 350°F, or until vigorous bubbles form around an inserted wooden chopstick. 

With a ladle, gently and slowly add 1/4 of the omelet batter. Egg foo young should immediately bubble and puff up like magic. Fry until golden brown and crispy on each side, about 2 minutes per side. If there are any light spots, use a ladle to gently baste it with hot oil.

Tip
Egg foo young can be a bit tricky to flip. The easiest method is to put a tool in each hand (a spider, slotted spoon, tongs, and large chopsticks are all good candidates) and gently coax the omelet over, pulling up on one side and pushing down and around on the other.

Remove the omelet and place it on a paper towel-lined baking sheet. Let it cool for 5 minutes. Meanwhile, repeat with the remaining batter to make 4 omelets. If needed, add more oil to the pan between batches.

Serve and enjoy:
Plate each egg foo young over a bed of rice. Spoon the warm gravy over the top and serve immediately.

ingredients.name: Unsalted Beef Stock
ingredients.assumptions: 1 cup beef stock, typical low-sodium canned or homemade value, mostly water with minimal nutrients.

ingredients.name: Soy Sauce
ingredients.assumptions: 1 tbsp regular soy sauce, standard sodium-fermented product.

ingredients.name: Shaoxing Wine
ingredients.assumptions: 1 tbsp Shaoxing rice wine, typical Chinese cooking wine values.

ingredients.name: Oyster Sauce
ingredients.assumptions: 1 tbsp oyster sauce, standard bottled Chinese variety.

ingredients.name: Pepper
ingredients.assumptions: 1/2 tsp white pepper powder, negligible contribution due to tiny amount.

ingredients.name: Cornstarch
ingredients.assumptions: 1 tbsp cornstarch, standard dry powder nutrition.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.assumptions: 1 tbsp water for gravy slurry, zero calories/macros.

ingredients.name: Cornstarch
ingredients.assumptions: 1 tbsp cornstarch for batter, standard dry powder nutrition.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.assumptions: 1 tbsp water for batter slurry, zero calories/macros.

ingredients.name: Egg
ingredients.assumptions: 8 large eggs (approx 50 g edible each, raw whole), standard large egg values.

ingredients.name: Kosher Salt
ingredients.assumptions: 1/2 tsp kosher salt, negligible contribution due to tiny amount.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.assumptions: 1/4 tsp granulated sugar, standard white sugar.

ingredients.name: Spring Onions
ingredients.assumptions: 1 spring onion (green onion), typical 15 g trimmed edible portion.

ingredients.name: Mung Bean Sprouts
ingredients.assumptions: 1 cup mung bean sprouts, standard raw volume-to-weight (104 g).

ingredients.name: Shrimp
ingredients.assumptions: 20 medium shrimp (peeled, deveined, raw); approx 5 g each edible meat, total 100 g.

ingredients.name: Vegetable Oil
ingredients.assumptions: 3 cups vegetable oil for deep frying; assumes ~100 g absorbed by the 4 omelets (typical 25 g oil per large egg foo young patty after draining; bulk of oil remains in wok and is not consumed).

ingredients.name: Jasmine Rice
ingredients.assumptions: 2 cups uncooked jasmine rice (standard dry volume-to-weight ~185 g per cup); rice is cooked and served as bed for the dish.
